claims.text: Uncomplicated pericarditis, first line: an NSAID (eg, ibuprofen 600–800 mg PO q6–8h), usually with colchicine.
claims.quote: First-line therapy for uncomplicated pericarditis is aspirin (325 to 650 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours) or another NSAID (eg, ibuprofen 600 to 800 mg orally every 6 to 8 hours), usually in combination with colchicine

claims.text: Consider a PPI for GI tolerability.
claims.quote: A proton pump inhibitor should be considered to improve the gastric tolerability of NSAIDs.

claims.text: A 3–4 wk course may lower recurrence (not well studied).
claims.quote: Risk of recurrence may be decreased with NSAID treatment if the duration of treatment is 3 to 4 weeks, but this approach has not been studied adequately.
